title: A Survey on Test-Time Scaling in Large Language Models: What, How, Where, and How Well?
actual_read_scope: Read the arXiv HTML v3 full article, including abstract, Sections 1-9, Tables 1-5, appendices A-B, and the complete reference list as rendered at https://arxiv.org/html/2503.24235. Version metadata was checked on the arXiv abstract page on 2026-09-09. No cited original paper was read.

routes.question: What is scaled?
routes.mechanism: Generate multiple responses in parallel, from one or multiple models, then select, vote, or fuse them; coverage and aggregation quality are separate factors.
routes.token_connection: Direct: increases sampled/generated reasoning tokens (or model calls) and trades pass@k/cons@k against token/FLOP cost.

routes.question: What is scaled?
routes.mechanism: Iteratively update an intermediate solution/state, using refinement, decomposition, self-correction, or repeated prompting.
routes.token_connection: Direct: adds serial reasoning tokens and rounds; coherence, error accumulation, and diminishing returns determine the useful budget.

routes.question: What is scaled?
routes.mechanism: Combine parallel expansion with sequential filtering/refinement; tree, graph, beam, MCTS, and multi-agent procedures explore and prune candidate states.
routes.token_connection: Direct: search branching and depth spend inference tokens; verifier quality and pruning determine whether extra compute improves the accuracy-token curve.

routes.question: What is scaled?
routes.mechanism: A tuned model autonomously generates hidden/intermediate states and learns a stopping policy, often through SFT/RL, instead of external orchestration.
routes.token_connection: Direct for generated thinking tokens, but allocation is endogenous; requires controllability and stopping analysis to avoid overthinking simple instances or underthinking hard ones.

routes.question: How is scaling implemented?
routes.mechanism: Outcome verification scores complete answers using verifier models, voting, discriminators, tools, heuristics, functional tests, or multi-agent evaluators; process verification scores intermediate states/steps with PRMs, state verifiers, self-evaluation, deductive checks, or tools.
routes.token_connection: Direct/indirect: verifier calls and candidate traces consume tokens; verification determines selection, search guidance, aggregation, and when to stop.

routes.question: How is scaling implemented?
routes.mechanism: Search organizes candidate reasoning states with DFS/BFS, beam, MCTS, graph or control-flow search; aggregation either selects a candidate (self-consistency, best-of-N, verifier score) or fuses multiple outputs.
routes.token_connection: Direct: search width/depth, candidate count, and aggregation calls define the inference-token budget; wrong discriminators can make additional search harmful.

routes.question: How are stopping and budgets handled?
routes.mechanism: External controls include max output length, fixed thinking-token budgets, budget forcing (suppressing end-of-thinking), and adaptive selection; internal models learn a halt policy. Verification can guide termination, but the survey identifies optimal stopping as unresolved.
routes.token_connection: Direct: controls the token axis of the performance-cost curve; controllability is measured by budget adherence and length deviation.

routes.question: How well does scaling work?
routes.mechanism: Report performance (Pass@1, Pass@k, Cons@k, pairwise win rate, task metrics), efficiency (tokens, FLOPs, latency, KV cache, reasoning-efficiency scores), controllability, and scalability.
routes.token_connection: Direct: scaling curves plot accuracy/pass rate versus token budgets, sample count, iterations, or total FLOPs; the survey highlights diminishing returns and saturation.

routes.question: How well does scaling spend tokens?
routes.mechanism: Reasoning efficiency is quality divided by computational cost; the survey distinguishes redundancy, underthinking, and overthinking, and defines underthinking, outcome-efficiency, and process-efficiency metrics.
routes.token_connection: Direct: diagnoses whether additional tokens produce correct answers, useful intermediate reasoning, or only repetition.

gaps_conflicts: The taxonomy is broad but stopping is not a dedicated route: the survey mentions learned halt policies, budget forcing, fixed max lengths, verification-guided stopping, and asks whether an optimal stopping criterion exists, without a unified stopping taxonomy or a closed-loop stop benchmark.

Scaling curves are defined conceptually (accuracy/pass rate versus tokens, samples, iterations, or FLOPs), but the survey does not standardize x-axis accounting across parallel samples, verifier calls, search overhead, KV-cache memory, latency, or model heterogeneity.

Pass@k/coverage, Cons@k/aggregation, and accuracy-compute curves are distinct; high coverage does not guarantee good selected output, and consensus can be wrong. The survey explicitly separates coverage from aggregation quality but does not resolve their causal decomposition.

The survey reports redundancy, underthinking, and overthinking as inefficiency patterns and gives metrics, yet most cited evidence is method- or task-specific; cross-domain calibration and comparable continuous token-performance traces remain open.

Internal scaling is jointly a post-training route and an inference behavior. SFT/RL, distillation, and warmup are training mechanisms rather than inference-token efficiency by themselves; they should not be interpreted as direct token savings without a matched test-time budget.

Some references have ambiguous or changing bibliographic identifiers in the rendered survey (for example, no arXiv ID is printed for s1, Brown et al., Muennighoff-linked metrics, Wang underthinking, and ETS); this extraction preserves only IDs explicitly printed in the survey or stable source pages and flags search URLs where the survey did not provide an ID.

Coverage stops at the survey's arXiv v3 revision on 2025-05-04. This assignment's 2026-09-09 verification confirms the fixed version, but no post-v3 literature was added and no original cited paper was independently read.
